notes.text:
This update for openssh fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-59995: sftp: a malicious server could change the the location of downloaded files (bsc#1271044).
- CVE-2026-59996: scp: a malicious server could write files to the parent directory of the intended target directory
  (bsc#1271046).
- CVE-2026-59997: sshd: internal-sftp command lines are silently truncated after the 9th argument (bsc#1271048).
- CVE-2026-59998: sshd: Undocumented GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck behavior impacts security in Windows Active Directory
  (bsc#1271049).
- CVE-2026-59999: sshd: DisableForwarding=yes didn't override PermitTunnel=yes (bsc#1271052).
- CVE-2026-60000: sshd: pre-authentication denial of service when GSSAPIAuthentication is enabled (bsc#1271053).
- CVE-2026-60001: sshd: honor the minimum authentication delay (bsc#1271054).
- CVE-2026-60002: ssh: client-side use-after-free when a server changes its host key during a key reexchange
  (bsc#1271055).
- CVE-2026-73281: refused binding requests on locked SSH agents can allow destination restriction bypasses
  (bsc#1275075).
- CVE-2026-73282: unsynchronized remote forwarding updates in SSH client multiplexing can cause use-after-free
  (bsc#1275074).
- CVE-2026-73283: unenforced restriction keywords on tunnel forwarding can allow administrative security policy bypasses
  (bsc#1275079).

notes.text: sftp in OpenSSH before 10.4 does not properly constrain the location of downloaded files when "sftp server:/path ." is used with an attacker-controlled server.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: scp in OpenSSH before 10.4 may place a file in the parent directory of an intended directory when the copy occurs between two remote destinations.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: internal-sftp in sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 recognizes only the first 9 command-line arguments, which can be important if a later command-line argument would have helped to ensure the intended security properties of an SFTP connection.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 has an undocumented security-relevant behavior: GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck has no value if the server is in Windows Active Directory.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4, DisableForwarding=yes was supposed to take precedence over PermitTunnel=yes, but did not.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (resource consumption from excessive authentication attempts) because MaxAuthTries was mishandled for GSSAPIAuthentication.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: sshd in OpenSSH before 10.4 does not always honor the minimum authentication delay.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: ssh in OpenSSH before 10.4 can have a use-after-free when a server changes its host key during a key re-exchange. (This outcome occurs only on the client side.)
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: In ssh-agent in OpenSSH before 10.5, some operations can occur remotely but were intended to occur only locally, including operations that add tokens or use keys. This is caused by misinteraction between agent locking and the session-bind@openssh.com extension.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: In ssh in OpenSSH before 10.5, a use-after-free for realloc data can occur if a certain pair of remote-forwarding operations are concurrent.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".

notes.text: In sshd in OpenSSH before 10.5, the restrict keyword (in authorized_keys) was supposed to be applicable to tunnel forwarding but was not.
notes.title: CVE description

remediations.details: To install this SUSE Security Update use the SUSE recommended installation methods like YaST online_update or "zypper patch".
